entry.title: On the Quantum Chromatic Gap II
entry.summary: We confirm a conjecture of the first author [SODA'26] on a strong form of pseudo-telepathy for Khot's $d$-to-$1$ games: for every $d\geq 4$, every $ε>0$, and every $k\in\mathbb N$, there is a $d$-to-$1$ label-cover game of classical value less than $ε$ that admits a perfect quantum strategy using finite-dimensional shared entanglement with measurement contexts of radius at least $k$. As a consequence, there exist graphs whose quantum chromatic number $χ_q$ is $3$ and whose classical chromatic number $χ$ is arbitrarily large. This is the first improvement on the quantum chromatic gap since the work of Brassard, Cleve, and Tapp [Phys. Rev. Lett.'99], which produced graphs for which $χ$ grows exponentially in $χ_q$. To prove the conjecture, we proceed as follows. We start with a ``stretched'' version of the Mermin--Peres magic square, obtained by spacing out its equations and linking them with additional long equation wires. This operation increases the radius of the initial measurement contexts of a perfect quantum strategy for the game, while preserving classical unsatisfiability. We then apply parallel repetition to make the classical value small, and we turn the system into a pseudo-telepathic multi-layered Kneser hypergraph via a PCP construction of Dinur, Guruswami, Khot, and Regev [STOC'03]. Finally, we feed the resulting hypergraph into the reduction of Fei, Minzer, and Wang from hypergraph colouring to $4$-to-$1$ games, we establish quantum completeness of this reduction, and we show that it preserves context radius.

entry.title: Real-rooted Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomials of crown posets and wheel and whirl matroids
entry.summary: We prove that the Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomials of crown order polytopes are real-rooted, settling a conjecture of Lundström and Saud Maia Leite. For each integer $r\ge3$, the crown order polytope on $2r$ elements and the rank-$r$ whirl base polytope have the same $h^*$-polynomial. The $h^*$-polynomials of the rank-$r$ wheel and whirl base polytopes, as well as every convex combination of the two, have $2r-2$ distinct negative roots. Their coefficient sequences are positive, unimodal, and strictly ultra log-concave of order $2r-2$.

entry.title: Thin ends and topological spanning trees
entry.summary: Halin conjectured in 1964 that every connected graph has an end-faithful spanning tree. He proved this for countable graphs, but in the early 1990s Seymour and Thomas and, independently, Thomassen found uncountable counterexamples. Both are infinitely connected and hence one-ended, and their unique end has uncountable degree (i.e.\ contains uncountably many pairwise disjoint rays). Several authors have since asked how much of the conjecture survives. Diestel asked in 1992 whether a graph has an end-faithful spanning tree as soon as all its one-ended connected subgraphs have one; by a theorem of Polat, this would give end-faithful spanning trees in all connected graphs whose ends have countable degree. Diestel and Kühn introduced topological spanning trees, a topological variant of end-faithful spanning trees that exists in every one-ended connected graph, and asked in 2004 whether every connected graph has one. And Carmesin asked in 2019 whether every graph has a spanning tree that is end-faithful at least for its thin ends, the ends of finite degree. We answer all three questions in the negative. We show that the uncountably chromatic graph from an earlier note of ours on a problem of Erdős and Hajnal has only ends of countable degree, each dominated by only countably many vertices, yet it has neither an end-faithful nor a topological spanning tree. A refinement of this graph moreover has no spanning tree that contains a ray from every end of degree~1.

entry.title: A p-adic Valuation Calculus for Permutations with Restricted Cycle Lengths
entry.summary: Let a_A(n) be the number of permutations of {1,...,n} all of whose cycle lengths lie in a set A. We develop a valuation calculus for these numbers. Mobius inversion writes the exponential generating function as an Euler product, and at a prime p the factors with non-p-integral exponents, the blocks, determine a finite knapsack problem. Its optimal value gives a lower bound for v_p(a_A(n)), and the bound is attained exactly when one residue modulo p, the sum of the terms of the optimal choices, does not vanish. For a fixed set A and prime p the bounds and residues for all n <= N cost O(N^2) operations. When one block is strictly the most efficient, the valuation inside each residue class is that of a locally analytic p-adic function. We use the calculus to determine the 2-adic and 3-adic valuations for cycle lengths at most 3, 4 and 5, to prove the divisibility conjectures recorded in A378495, A079128, A193437 and A193438 and the 3-adic statements recorded in A057693 and A070945, and to treat 99 OEIS sequences in all. We also prove sharp divisibility and gcd theorems, show that at n = 111 the gcd of the counts over all sets of excluded cycle lengths containing {1,2,3} is one third of the gcd over the sets {1,2,3,k}, and determine eventual divisibility and tail gcds modulo composite integers. Part of the paper is formalized in Lean 4.
entry.arxiv:comment: 62 pages. Ancillary files: verification scripts and outputs, Lean 4 sources, and an OEIS catalogue of 99 sequences

entry.title: Computer-Assisted Results for \(n\)-Sided Non-Transitive Dice Taking Face Values in \([n]\)
entry.summary: We consider non-transitivity among dice with \(n\) sides restricted to taking face values in the set \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\). We give a computer-assisted proof that \(n=6\) is the smallest \(n\ge3\) which admits a non-transitive cycle of maximum length \(n\) with uniform and minimal winning advantage. For \(n=6\), we identify the two unique non-transitive cycles of length \(6\). We present computational evidence supporting a conjecture that \(n=6\) is the largest \(n\ge3\) which admits a non-transitive cycle of maximum length \(n\) with uniform and minimal winning advantage.
entry.arxiv:comment: 59 pages, 6 figures. Appendix includes Julia code and computational output

entry.title: The Borodin--Kostochka Conjecture for Two Classes of Diamond-Free Graphs
entry.summary: We prove the Borodin--Kostochka conjecture for $(\mathrm{diamond},L_4)$-free graphs and $(\mathrm{diamond},K_5^+)$-free graphs, where $L_4$ is obtained from $K_4$ by attaching a path of length two to one clique vertex, and $K_5^+$ is obtained from $K_5$ by adding a vertex adjacent to exactly one clique vertex. The proof uses structural properties of maximum cliques in diamond-free vertex-critical graphs with $χ=Δ$.

entry.title: On separators in $K_t$-minor-free graphs
entry.summary: This manuscript presents a proof of the Alon--Seymour--Thomas conjecture developed under the author's guidance using ChatGPT 6pro. The author has checked every formula and theorem by hand and used Codex to assist with writing. GPT 6.1 Sol (Max) was also used to check the proof repeatedly and to generate numerous examples for verification. More precisely, for every integer $h\geq3$, every $n$-vertex $K_h$-minor-free graph has a vertex set of size at most $\min{n,21h\sqrt n}$ whose deletion leaves every component with at most $2n/3$ vertices.

entry.title: Packing and covering random trees
entry.summary: We study the sizes of optimal packings and coverings of conditioned branching processes by balls with growing radii. We find a universal limiting constant, and thereby establish universality of packing and covering numbers across different scales and different offspring distributions. To be precise, for $μ$ an offspring distribution with mean $1$ and finite variance $σ^2$ we let $T_n$ be a Bienaymé tree with offspring distribution $μ$ conditioned to have size $n$. We prove that the packing number (resp. covering number) of $T_n$ with balls of radii $1\ll γ_n \ll n^{1/2}$ is asymptotically equivalent to $\mathfrak{C} n /(σ^2 γ_n^2)$ (resp. $\mathfrak{C} n /(4σ^2 γ_n^2)$), for a universal constant $\mathfrak{C}$. We also show that the order of limits can be exchanged and that the same limit occurs when we first consider the limiting covering number of $T_n$ by balls of fixed radius $R$, and thereafter let $R$ tend to $\infty$. We then extend these results to the Brownian continuum random tree conditioned to have mass $1$. For this model, we prove that the packing (resp. covering) number with balls of radii $\varepsilon$ are asymptotically equivalent to $\mathfrak{C}/\varepsilon^2$ (resp. $\mathfrak{C}/(4\varepsilon^2)$), for the same constant $\mathfrak{C}$, in contrast with a conjecture by Aldous. Finally, our results answer a question by Devroye, Eide and Pralat on the asymptotic burning number of mean $1$ finite variance Bienaymé trees of size $n$, by showing that it lies between $(c+o(1)) n^{1/3}$ and $(2c+o(1))n^{1/3}$ with high probability, for a constant $c$ that only depends on the offspring variance.

entry.title: A lifted entropy splitting lemma and applications
entry.summary: We give a matrix lifting of the entropy-splitting theorem of Csiszár, Körner, Lovász, Marton, and Simonyi, and show several applications. We use it to prove the Cartesian-product inequality conjectured by Sinjorgo and Sotirov for the generalized Lovász theta number, and we also answer the saturation and convexification questions of Carli Silva, Coutinho, Oliveira, and Tunçel on the same theme. For the strong Hoffman bound, we answer a question of Wocjan, Elphick, and Darbari concerning orthogonal rank, and show that optimization over matrix weights gives exactly the ceiling of the theta number of the complement. Finally, we extend the lifting to diagonally invariant cones of positive semidefinite matrices, giving a proof of a conjecture by Kuryatnikova, Sotirov, and Vera, and giving a short proof, for all graphs, of a theta-based weakening of Fajtlowicz's graph-energy conjecture.

entry.title: The bivariate generating function for cylindric partitions of rank three
entry.summary: Using a rational analogue of an $\mathrm{A}_2^{(1)}$ Rogers--Ramanujan type identity discovered by Warnaar, we establish sum-like expressions for a bivariate generating function for cylindric partitions of rank three. These expressions provide the finishing touch towards conjectures of Warnaar and Kanade--Russell.

entry.title: Quasimodularity of $q$-series associated to root lattices
entry.summary: Motivated by conjectures arising in part from the study of class-$\mathcal{S}$ vertex algebras associated with four-dimensional supersymmetric field theories, we study multiple $q$-zeta functions attached to finite-dimensional simple Lie algebras. We prove their conjectured quasimodularity for all classical Lie algebras of types $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$, as well as a more general Weyl-symmetrized version in which the exponents attached to the positive roots are allowed to vary, under a suitable parity condition. Our proof is based on a substantially more general result. We introduce new combinatorial objects, called sets of level one and pairs of level two, which generalize the configurations arising from classical root systems. To these we associate multivariable lattice sums and prove that, under a natural admissibility condition, they are Fourier expansions of polar quasi-Jacobi forms of level one and level two, respectively. Quasimodularity of the Lie-theoretic $q$-series follows by specialization of the elliptic variables. The positive roots of type $A$ form a set of level one, and those of types $B$, $C$, and $D$ are described by pairs of level two. The proof combines a structural analysis of these new combinatorial configurations with reduction procedures and induction on the rank. The resulting framework applies to a much wider class of lattice sums than those coming from root systems and supports more general quasimodularity conjectures for $q$-series associated with integral hyperplane arrangements.

entry.title: On the maximum interval index of a graph
entry.summary: For a connected graph P G on n vertices, the interval index is defined by Int(G) = {u,v} subset V(G) (|I(u, v)| - 1), where I(u, v) denotes the set of all vertices lying on a shortest u - v path. It was conjectured that, among all connected graphs on n vertices, the path Pn attains the maximum value of the interval index. In this paper we settle this conjecture, and we prove that the maximum is attained only for Pn, except for n = 4, when the cycle C4 attains the same value. We also prove that, for every n >= 31, the maximum interval index among graphs without pendant vertices equals (n^3 - n)/6 - 2(n - 4) and it is attained by a dumbbell graph, obtained by joining two 4-cycles by a path.

entry.title: EPPA for Reducts of the Random Graph
entry.summary: We prove that finite two-graphs have coherent EPPA and that neither graphs modulo global complementation nor two-graphs modulo global complementation have EPPA. This completes the classification of EPPA and coherent EPPA for the reducts of the random graph, answering a question and confirming a conjecture of Evans, Hubička, Konečný and Nešetřil.

entry.title: Symbolic depth functions of edge ideals via local graph structure
entry.summary: We study the depth of symbolic powers of edge ideals, focusing on local properties of graphs. First, we give several sufficient conditions for the symbolic depth function to be non-increasing, using local properties of graphs and local cohomology. Next, we give a counterexample to a conjecture of Minh, T.N. Trung, and Vu concerning the stable value of the symbolic depth function, where the difference between the conjectured value and the actual value can be arbitrary large. Finally, we study a conjecture of Muta stating the depth of a symbolic power of an edge ideal is at least that of the corresponding ordinary power. We prove it for graphs whose connected components are unicyclic or bipartite.

entry.title: The complete existence spectrum of periodic complementary ternary pairs of weight nine
entry.summary: For two sequences with entries $0,\pm1$, periodic complementarity means that their periodic autocorrelation functions sum to zero at every nonzero shift. We give necessary and sufficient conditions on the length for the existence of such pairs of total weight nine, where weight counts nonzero entries. The conditions decide existence at any prescribed length by divisibility tests. The main new result bounds the length of primitive pairs with two nonzero components. A pair is primitive if it cannot be shortened by removing uniformly inserted zeros after independent cyclic permutations. We prove primitive-length bounds of $64,48,64$ for weight distributions $(5,4),(6,3),(7,2)$. These bounds make the classification finite and prove that the earlier searches contain every required case. Exhaustive enumeration gives $91$ primitive sequence-equivalence classes. Including the five known circulant classes gives $96$ representatives from which every pair can be generated. The same catalogue gives class counts at every length. For constructing one pair, $33$ displayed seeds suffice. The results settle earlier conjectures on the weight distributions and decide exactly which orders admit the associated two-circulant weighing-matrix construction.

entry.title: $e$-Positive caterpillars have maximum degree at most three
entry.summary: Dahlberg, She, and van Willigenburg conjectured that every $e$-positive tree has maximum degree at most three. We prove this conjecture for caterpillars. Our proof introduces a specialization--cone method: we evaluate chromatic symmetric functions under finite-support specializations that are nonnegative on the elementary symmetric functions, express the evaluations through transfer matrices, and certify negativity using finitely generated cones. Two specializations and three cones handle all caterpillars remaining after a connected-partition reduction, with no bound on the number or spacing of their trivalent vertices. The required cone inclusions and strict sign inequalities are certified by exact rational arithmetic. We also exhibit two infinite families of non-spider caterpillars of maximum degree four that admit connected partitions of every type, showing that Wolfgang's criterion alone leaves cases requiring further obstructions. Our result also reduces Li's criterion on $e$-positivity for caterpillars of maximum degree three to an explicit condition on the positions of trivalent vertices.

entry.title: The maximum number of triangles in regular graphs
entry.summary: We determine the maximum number of triangles in $n$-vertex $k$-regular graphs and characterize all extremal graphs for all admissible orders when $k$ is odd and for an explicit range of orders when $k$ is even. For even $k$, we also give explicit lower and upper bounds for the remaining orders. As a consequence, we obtain a lower bound on the number of independent sets of size three in $k$-regular graphs and characterize all equality cases. Our exact results confirm the conjecture of Petingi and Rodríguez and the triangle case of a conjecture of Cambie, de Joannis de Verclos and Kang for all odd $k$ and the specified orders when $k$ is even. Moreover, for every even $k\ge18$, we construct counterexamples to both conjectures and obtain a recursive characterization of all extremal graphs of order at least $Ck$, where $C$ is an absolute constant.

entry.title: Linear hereditary quasirandomness
entry.summary: Conlon, Fox and Sudakov (\emph{Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc.} \textbf{164} (2018), 385--399) conjectured that hereditary subgraph counts force quasirandomness with linear dependence on the counting error. We prove this for every graph containing an edge. Let \(H\) have \(r\) vertices and \(m\ge1\) edges, and fix \(p\in(0,1)\). If every subset \(S\) of an \(n\)-vertex graph \(G\) contains \(p^m|S|^r\pmδn^r\) labelled injective copies of \(H\), then \(\lvert e_G(A,B)-p|A||B|\rvert\le C_{H,p}δn^2\) for all \(A,B\subseteq V(G)\), where \(e_G(A,B)\) counts ordered adjacent pairs. The proof extracts averaged rooted counts and represents each nonlinear term by a linear map in one selected edge factor. Composing two such maps gives an edge substitution with a superlinear cut-norm bound. A separate star expansion gives stronger local estimates for triangle-free graphs. The linear order is best possible even when \(2e(G)/n^2=p+O(n^{-2})\).

entry.title: Error terms for sums of two linear transformations
entry.summary: Let $d$ be a positive integer, and let $\mathcal L_1,\mathcal L_2$ be irreducible and coprime linear transformations from $\mathbb{Z}^d$ to $\mathbb{Z}^d$. In this paper, we prove that, for every finite nonempty set $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^d$, \[ |\mathcal L_1A+\mathcal L_2A| \ge \left(|\det\mathcal L_1|^{1/d}+|\det\mathcal L_2|^{1/d}\right)^d|A|-O\left(|A|^{1-1/d}\right). \] This confirms the conjecture of Conlon and Lim on the error term for two linear transformations.

entry.title: Some results on intersecting families of triangulations
entry.summary: Kalai conjectured that the largest intersecting family of triangulations of an $n$-gon is the family consisting of all triangulations that contain a fixed ear (a chord of length $2$). What happens if we strengthen the intersecting condition to the condition that any two of the triangulations must intersect on a chord from a specified family of chords -- for example, what if any two triangulations intersect on a chord from some fixed point of the $n$-gon, or intersect on an ear? In this paper we verify Kalai's conjecture for families of triangulations in which any two intersect on a chord from some fixed point. We also show that any ear-intersecting family of triangulations has size at most $T_{n-1} +T_{n-3} = T_{n-1}(17/16 + o(1))$, where $T_{n-1}$ is the upper bound in Kalai's conjecture, namely the number of triangulations of an $(n-1)$-gon. This is based on an exact upper bound of $T_{n-1}$ for the size of a family of triangulations in which any two intersect on some ear from the set of all ears with one ear excluded.

entry.title: A proof of the Murty--Simon conjecture on diameter-$2$-critical graphs
entry.summary: The Murty-Simon conjecture states that every $n$-vertex diameter-$2$-critical graph has at most $\lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor$ edges, with equality only for the balanced complete bipartite graph. Using regularity methods, Füredi proved this for all sufficiently large $n$ (specifically, $n$ greater than a tower of $2$'s of height roughly $10^{14}$). We present a proof of the Murty-Simon conjecture that works for all $n$. A proof of the $\lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor$ bound was originally found by AI; we simplified this proof and extended its ideas to get a proof of the full conjecture.

entry.title: Hook monomial immanants are Kazhdan-Lusztig positive
entry.summary: Stembridge conjectured that every monomial immanant is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices, and Haiman proposed a stronger statement which at $q=1$ says that every monomial immanant is a non-negative integer combination of the Kazhdan-Lusztig immanants of Rhoades and Skandera. We prove this for every hook shape $(a,1^{n-a})$ and every $n$. More precisely, each of the per-vertex functions obtained by splitting Stembridge's formula for hook characters is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive. The main tool is a positivity statement for products: a product of Kazhdan-Lusztig positive immanants of complementary submatrices is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive, which we deduce at $q=1$ from Braden's hyperbolic localization, following Billey and Braden. With Haiman's theorem for irreducible characters, it shows that every class function whose Frobenius characteristic lies in the semiring generated by Schur functions and hook monomial symmetric functions is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive; for example, Skandera's chain of normalised hook immanants is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive for every $n$. We place these results in a comparison of three cones of class functions, and show that the remaining obstructions to Haiman's conjecture lie at singular Schubert varieties that are not reached by an iterated doubling identity of Abreu and Nigro, for which we give an explicit criterion. Finally, on the full span of permutation monomials, an element that is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices can have a negative coefficient at the Kazhdan-Lusztig immanant $\mathrm{Imm}_w$ if and only if the Schubert variety $X_w$ is singular; Skandera proved the smooth half.
entry.arxiv:comment: 24 pages, 7 figures, 1 table. Code and data: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23730750

entry.title: The bigraded Frobenius series of the wreath product superspace coinvariant rings
entry.summary: We determine the bigraded Frobenius series of the superspace coinvariant ring $R^{(1,1)}_{\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n}$ for the wreath products $\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n$, which is the quotient of the ring $\mathbb{C}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\otimes\bigwedge[θ_1,\ldots,θ_n]$ of polynomial-valued differential forms by the ideal generated by diagonal $\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n$-invariants with vanishing constant term. The bigraded multiplicity of each irreducible character is a sum over standard Young $r$-tableaux of an expression determined by the flag major index and flag descent number. This refines the Frobenius series graded by fermionic degree found by Bhattacharya--Rhoades (2026). It specializes at $r=2$ to the hyperoctahedral group $\mathfrak{B}_n$ case, and it specializes at $r=1$ to recover the theorem of Murai--Rhoades--Wilson (2025) on the symmetric group $\mathfrak{S}_n$. We give new formulas for the bigraded multiplicities of hook characters of the superspace coinvariant ring in types $A$ and $B$, yielding upper bounds on trigraded multiplicities of the sign character of $R^{(1,2)}_{\mathfrak{S}_n}$ and the determinant character of $R^{(1,2)}_{\mathfrak{B}_n}$. As a corollary, we deduce a conjecture of F. Bergeron (2024) on hook components of $R^{(1,1)}_{\mathfrak{S}_n}$.

entry.title: All-even sets in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and $\mathbb{R}^3$
entry.summary: Call a finite nonempty point set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ all-even if for every direction $\ell \in \mathbb{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$, the number of hyperplanes perpendicular to $\ell$ that intersect $S$ is even. In 2026, Francisco Santos presented a question of Juan Benigno Seoane-Sepúlveda on the existence of all-even sets in dimensions $3$ and higher, together with examples of such sets in dimension $2$. Call a set $S\in\mathbb{R}^d$ line-all-even if for every direction $\ell \in \mathbb{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ the number of lines parallel to $\ell$ that intersect $S$ is even. As Santos pointed out, every all-even set in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is line-all-even. We conjecture that there exist no line-all-even sets in $\mathbb{R}^3$ that affinely span $\mathbb{R}^3$ We show that our conjecture is equivalent to the statement that every planar all-even set satisfies a certain property, which we call height-rigidity. This property has a natural interpretation in linear algebra terms. Furthermore, we present a hierarchy of properties of planar point sets that imply height-rigidity. We construct several all-even sets in the plane, including some infinite families, and show that all the sets we constructed are height-rigid. In addition, we prove that every all-even set in the plane that can be covered by six or fewer parallel lines is height-rigid.

entry.title: Extended weak order in all rank three Coxeter groups
entry.summary: We prove that extended weak order is a lattice for all rank 3 Coxeter groups. This was previously known in finite and affine types, and in the universal Coxeter group of rank 3. All other cases are new to this paper. As in earlier work, the proof proceeds by showing that all rank 3 Coxeter arrangements are clean arrangements, meaning that every biclosed set is weakly separated from its complement by a hyperplane. As a consequence, we also deduce Dyer's Conjecture A for all rank 3 Coxeter groups, which asserts that cover relations in extended weak order are given by toggling a single root.

entry.title: Primitive flag-transitive generalized quadrangles
entry.summary: Let $\mathcal{Q}$ be a finite thick generalized quadrangle of order $(s,t)$ with a flag-transitive automorphism group $G$. A well-known conjecture of Kantor from the early 1990s asserts that up to duality, $\mathcal{Q}$ is either of classical type, or it is one of two sporadic examples of order $(3,5)$ or $(15,17)$. Although this fundamental problem in finite geometry remains open, it has been resolved in some special cases. For example, a theorem of Buekenhout and Van Maldeghem from 1994 proves Kantor's conjecture under the stronger assumption that $G$ acts distance-transitively on the set of points of $\mathcal{Q}$. In this paper, we study Kantor's conjecture in the setting where $G$ acts primitively on both the points and lines of $\mathcal{Q}$. Here a theorem of Bamberg et al. implies that $G$ is almost simple with socle $X$ a finite simple group of Lie type, and several special cases where the Lie rank of $X$ is at most $2$ have recently been settled in a sequence of papers. Our main theorem resolves the problem for all almost simple groups of Lie type, thereby completing the proof of Kantor's conjecture for generalized quadrangles with a flag-transitive automorphism group acting primitively on points and lines.

entry.title: Large tight components and Dirac thresholds for tight Hamilton cycles
entry.summary: For every odd integer $r\ge1$, let $q_r=1-2^{-r}\binom r{(r-1)/2}$. We show that, for every odd $r\ge3$ and sufficiently large $n$, every $n$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraph with at least $q_r\binom nr$ edges contains a tight component with at least $(1/2-o(1))\binom nr$ edges. This confirms a conjecture posed by Lang and Sanhueza-Matamala in 2024. As an application, for every odd $r\ge1$ and every integer $k\ge\lceil r(3-2q_r)\rceil$, we prove that the asymptotic minimum $(k-r)$-degree threshold for a tight Hamilton cycle in a $k$-uniform hypergraph is $q_r$, which settles, in this range, another conjecture of Lang and Sanhueza-Matamala in 2022 stating that the lower-bound construction due to Han and Zhao is asymptotically optimal. Our proof combines an isoperimetric inequality for Johnson graphs with a Kruskal-Katona-type theorem, which is of independent interest.

entry.title: The asymptotics of off-diagonal book Ramsey numbers
entry.summary: Let $B_n$ be the book graph consisting of $n$ triangles sharing a common edge. We prove upper bounds for $r(B_{\lceilαn\rceil},B_n)$ that asymptotically match the known lower bounds in the remaining range $1/6<α<1/4$. Combined with the known results for the other ranges of $α$, this completely determines the asymptotics of the Ramsey number $r(B_{\lceilαn\rceil},B_n)$ for every fixed $0<α\le1$: \[ r(B_{\lceilαn\rceil},B_n)=(c(α)+o(1))n, \qquad c(α)= \begin{cases} 2, & 0<α\le1/6,\\[1mm] \displaystyle\frac{3}{1+2p_α^2}, & 1/6<α\leα_0,\\[3mm] (1+\sqrtα)^2, & α_0<α\le1, \end{cases} \] where \(α_0:=\frac{52-16\sqrt3}{121}, \;\; p_α:=\frac{1-\sqrt{α(3-2α)}}{1-2α} \;\; (1/6<α\leα_0).\) Consequently, the random lower bound is asymptotically tight if and only if $α\geα_0$, thereby determining exactly the range of $α$ for which the conjecture of Conlon, Fox and Wigderson holds. The proof develops a defect-compensation framework around a $K_4$-free auxiliary graph.

entry.title: Hilbert functions of filtered graphical zonotopal algebras
entry.summary: The external zonotopal algebra of a graph is generated by nilpotent vertex elements $X_v$ and determines the graphical matroid after deleting loops. Replacing these generators by $f(X_v)$, for a power series $f(u)$, and filtering by word length gives a family of filtered algebras. We extend filtered graph reconstruction from simple graphs to loopless multigraphs without isolated vertices when the linear and quadratic coefficients of $f$ are nonzero. Nevertheless, even the family of Hilbert functions indexed by all polynomials does not determine the graph: two nonisomorphic ten-vertex trees have the same Hilbert function for every $f$, answering a question of Nenashev and the first author. For forests and series whose first nonconstant term has degree $k\ge 2$, we give a monomial presentation indexed by partial score vectors whose entries are divisible by $k$. For normalized nondegenerate functions, a boundary-state calculus gives a common finite parameter partition for all trees of a fixed maximum degree. In maximum degrees three and four, exact symbolic calculations identify these partitions by the vanishing of specified coefficients of $f^{-1}$. For functions with nonzero quadratic coefficient, the same calculus gives explicit recurrences for attached or connecting paths. Symmetry reductions, including commuting actions of $sl_2$ and the symmetric group on the leaves of a star, determine the generic Hilbert series of stars and two-vertex multigraphs and also apply to parallel edges and leaves in larger graphs. For cycles, we determine the highest-degree term and the first three nonconstant coefficients in the stable range. A weighted independent-set formula describes the trace sequence in the remaining conjecture.

entry.title: Nice Partitions of Signed-Graphic Arrangements Are Inductive Factorizations
entry.summary: Nice partitions of hyperplane arrangements give tensor factorizations of Orlik-Solomon algebras as graded vector spaces. In general, a hyperplane arrangement admitting a nice partition need not be free. In this paper, we consider signed-graphic arrangements, the subarrangements of type-$B$ Weyl arrangements, over fields of characteristic different from $2$. We prove that every nice partition of a signed-graphic arrangement is an inductive factorization and hence that the arrangement is free, with nonzero exponents given by the part sizes. In particular, Terao's conjecture holds for the intersection lattices of signed-graphic arrangements admitting a nice partition.

entry.title: High-chromatic tournament parts without a complete pair of cyclic triangles
entry.summary: Nguyen, Scott, and Seymour conjectured that any two disjoint subtournaments of sufficiently large chromatic number contain cyclic triangles, one in each subtournament, with all edges between them oriented in the same direction. We disprove this conjecture by constructing, for every positive integer $d$, a tournament $T$ with a vertex partition $(X,Y)$ such that $χ(T[X]),χ(T[Y])\ge d$, but no cyclic triangle in either part is complete to a cyclic triangle in the other. Our construction combines a graph of large girth and large chromatic number with a variant of Kneser graphs defined in terms of binary functions. We give two proofs of the required chromatic lower bound, one using the Borsuk--Ulam theorem and the other using the octahedral form of Tucker's lemma.

entry.title: Homotopy types and torsion in homology of generalized chessboard complexes
entry.summary: Multiple chessboard complexes are deleted joins of skeleta of a simplex. We classify their homotopy types for at most three rows and extend this classification to arbitrary column capacities, with the $2$-torus as the only exception to a wedge of spheres. We determine explicit homotopy decompositions for two families with four and five rows and use a common capacity redistribution map to construct infinite families with $2$- and $3$-torsion in integral homology. Together, these results give a negative answer to the Segre part of the problem posed by Reiner and Roberts on characteristic-free resolutions of Segre and Veronese modules and identify three as the largest number of rows for which all generalized chessboard complexes have torsion-free integral homology. Our $3$-torsion construction applies to every square ordinary chessboard complex with at least five rows. Combined with earlier results, it completes the proof of the Shareshian-Wachs conjecture on torsion in chessboard complexes.

entry.title: Generic tensor products are not maximal
entry.summary: We construct tensor products of uniform matroids which are strictly freer than their generic linear tensor products. In particular, the generic tensor product of two copies of $U_{7,9}$ is not maximal. More generally, for every $a,b\ge2$, this holds for $U_{7,a+7}$ and $U_{7,b+7}$. The construction disproves the uniform tensor-product formulation of Mason's conjecture. Its dual is a relaxation of an explicit circuit-hyperplane of a generic birigidity matroid. By the author's representability theorem, the resulting matroids are non-representable over every field. We also obtain full-rank counterexamples to the Jackson--Tanigawa hyperconnectivity conjecture in every dimension $d\ge2$.

entry.title: A cubic chromatic bound for capped graphs
entry.summary: An ordered graph is capped if, for any four vertices $a<b<c<d$, the edges $ac$ and $bd$ imply the edge $ad$. We prove that every nonempty capped graph $G$ satisfies $χ(G)\leq\min\{3^{ω(G)-1},18ω(G)^3\}$, where $χ(G)$ and $ω(G)$ are its chromatic number and clique number. This proves a conjecture of Davies, Krawczyk, McCarty and Walczak.

entry.title: Coprime matchings of divisor sets
entry.summary: For a positive integer $n$, let $D(n)$ be its set of positive divisors and put $N:=τ(n)=|D(n)|$. We characterize the arithmetic progressions $\mathcal P$ of length $N$ that admit a bijection with $D(n)$ pairing relatively prime integers. Such a coprime matching exists if and only if, for every prime $p\mid n$, at most $N/(ν_p(n)+1)$ terms of $\mathcal P$ are divisible by $p$, where $ν_p(n)$ is the exponent of $p$ in $n$. Call $n$ an $M$-number if $p^p\nmid n$ for every prime $p$. We prove that $D(n)$ can be matched with every primitive arithmetic progression of length $N$, meaning one whose first term and common difference are coprime, if and only if $n$ is an $M$-number. This proves a conjecture of McNew and Pomerance. We call $n$ \emph{matchable} if $D(n)$ admits a coprime matching with the primitive arithmetic progression $\{1,2,\ldots,N\}$. The general criterion implies that $n$ is matchable if and only if $\lfloor N/p\rfloor\le N/(ν_p(n)+1)$ for all $p\mid n$. We explicitly classify the matchable non-$M$-numbers, settle a conjectured divisor criterion, and prove that every divisor of a matchable integer is matchable. A Vandermonde determinant gives the required matchings under bounds on the prime exponents, while a partition into shorter progressions handles the remaining cases.

entry.title: Sharp Bounds for Toral Eigenfunctions and Threefold Additive Energy on Circles
entry.summary: For the lattice circle $P_n=\{z\in\mathbb{Z}^2:|z|^2=n\}$, we prove that the threefold additive energy $J_3(P_n)\le C|P_n|^3$, with an absolute constant $C$. This establishes the optimal bound suggested by Krishnapur--Kurlberg--Wigman and Bombieri--Bourgain. We also prove a uniform weak $L^6$ bound for $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions on the square torus, and hence uniform $L^p$ bounds for every $1\le p<6$. This extends the classical $L^4$ bounds of Cooke and Zygmund and establishes Bourgain's conjecture in this range. Applications include mean-square convergence for $L^{6/5}$ observables and a logarithm-free remainder in the nodal length variance of arithmetic random waves.

entry.title: Toric Varieties from Multiple Zeta Values
entry.summary: The linear relations among fixed weight multiple zeta values (MZVs) are a well-studied subject in number theory. Elements of putative linear bases for this fixed-weight space are, however, not algebraically independent; they satisfy non-linear relations. We study these relations by approximating them through motivic MZVs, formal MZVs and numerical computations. We show that motivic MZVs in fixed weight span a projective toric variety and explore its geometry. We define an outer approximation to the variety of formal MZVs in fixed weight by introducing toric varieties coming from shuffle and stuffle relations and taking their intersection. We conjecture that this intersection in fact agrees with the variety of formal MZVs and hence conjecturally also with the variety of motivic MZVs. This leads to a novel conjecture on a generating set for the extended double shuffle relations, which we checked computationally up to weight $23$.

entry.title: Non-convergence in heterogeneous Hegselmann-Krause dynamics: The bounded influence model
entry.summary: In a recent preprint, we found counterexamples to a number of auxiliary conjectures in a 2012 paper of Mirtabatabaei and Bullo, concerning convergence in two fundamental models of heterogeneous Hegselmann-Krause dynamics, the synchronized bounded confidence (SBC) and synchronized bounded influence (SBI) models. Building on our work, Etesami and Touri presented an example of an opinion vector which doesn't converge under SBC dynamics, resolving the main conjecture from the 2012 paper in that case. Here we complete this project by presenting an example of an opinion vector which doesn't converge under SBI dynamics. The example was found with the help of AI.

entry.title: Optimal path decompositions of sparse random graphs
entry.summary: Let $\operatorname{odd}(G)$ be the number of odd-degree vertices of a graph $G$. We prove that, if $p=o(1)$ and $np/\log n\to\infty$, then with probability tending to one the random graph $G(n,p)$ has an edge decomposition into exactly $\operatorname{odd}(G)/2$ paths. This confirms a conjecture of Glock, Kühn and Osthus from 2016. The proof combines a key lemma with cycle decompositions of random graphs.

entry.title: Enumeration of zero-sum subsequences: A proof of Bialostocki-Lotspeich conjecture
entry.summary: Let $C_n$ be a cyclic group of order $n\ge 2$, and let $S=g_1\cdot\ldots\cdot g_{\ell}$ be a sequence over $C_n$, with repetitions allowed. We denote by $\mathsf N_0^n(S)$ the number of subsets $I\subseteq[1,\ell]$ with $|I|=n$ and $\sum_{i\in I}g_i=0$. A conjecture proposed by Bialostocki and Lotspeich in 1992 states that $$\mathsf N_0^n(S)\ge \binom{\lfloor |S|/2\rfloor}{n}+ \binom{\lceil |S|/2\rceil}{n}.$$ Several partial results toward this conjecture are known. In this paper, we prove this conjecture completely.

entry.title: Factorizations by column blocks and Schubert polynomials as products of key polynomials
entry.summary: We classify the Schubert polynomials that are products of key polynomials and explicitly determine their finest key factorization. Their indexing permutations are precisely those avoiding ten classical patterns of length six, which form the minimal pattern basis. More generally, the connected components of the column interaction graph give the unique finest factorization of a dual flagged Weyl character into nonconstant diagram characters. Every other such factorization is obtained by grouping these components. We also prove Makhija's conjecture on products of elementary symmetric polynomials in initial alphabets, allowing repeated alphabets. In this case, the elementary factors are uniquely determined, up to order, by the nonempty Rothe columns.

entry.title: A characterization of equality in the edge-localized Bollobás-Nikiforov inequality
entry.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph of order $n\ge2$. Let $e(G)$ and $ω(G)$ denote its number of edges and clique number, respectively. Let $λ_1(G)\ge\cdots\geλ_n(G)$ be its adjacency eigenvalues. In 2007, Bollobás and Nikiforov conjectured that every graph $G\neq K_n$ satisfies $λ_1^2(G)+λ_2^2(G)\le2\left(1-\frac1{ω(G)}\right)e(G).$ This conjecture was recently completely resolved by Coutinho, Liu, Spier, Tang and Zhang. For every edge $e\in E(G)$, let $c_G(e)$ denote the maximum order of a clique containing $e$. Kannan, Kumar and Pragada proposed the edge-localized conjecture $λ_1^2(G)+λ_2^2(G)\le2\sum_{e\in E(G)}\left(1-\frac1{c_G(e)}\right)$ for every graph $G\neq K_n$. This conjecture was subsequently proved by Shaik. In this paper, we provide complete structural characterizations of the equality cases in both the Bollobás-Nikiforov inequality and its edge-localized version.

entry.title: Jack multiple zeta function
entry.summary: For conjugate shapes $λ$ and $λ'$, Stanley's duality relates the Jack symmetric functions $J_λ(x;α)$ and $J_{λ'}(x;1/α)$. Through Stanley's combinatorial formula, it is an identity between the sums of the weights of the semi-standard Young tableaux giving the same monomial. We introduce the Jack multiple zeta functions, which keep these weights separate, and prove that Stanley's duality lifts to them, including the case of skew shapes. Thus the duality holds before the weights are summed up, and in fact step by step along chains of partitions. Since the duality is an identity among formal symbols, the same duality holds when the multiple zeta functions are replaced by other functions, and replacing them with the monomial quasi-symmetric functions recovers Stanley's duality. Hence our duality is a refinement of Stanley's duality which contains it as a special case. In particular, we obtain a duality for the Schur multiple zeta functions and the classical relation between the multiple zeta and zeta-star functions. We next show that any expansion of a Jack symmetric function in terms of Schur functions can be lifted to Jack multiple zeta functions, yielding an analog of a formula conjectured by Stanley and proved by Koike. We also show that the Jack multiple zeta functions of one-row shape give a one-parameter family interpolating the multiple zeta and zeta-star functions, and we discuss their values at $\{2\}^r$ and at $\{2\}^a,3,\{2\}^b$.

entry.title: Diameter Bounds and Finiteness of Graphs from Local Intersection Data
entry.summary: We extend the Bakry--Émery curvature framework on graphs, broadening its applications and strengthening the resulting diameter bounds. We study diameter bounds and finiteness for amply regular graphs, distance-regular graphs, $(s,c,a,k)$-graphs, and locally strongly regular graphs. In particular, for an amply regular graph with parameters $(v,k,λ,μ)$, we prove that \[{\rm{diam}}(G)\le4+8\log\frac{k}{λ+2}\] when $μ>2$ and $k\ge3λ^2/μ$, improving the previous linear bound $4k/(λ+4)$ to a logarithmic bound. We also address several related conjectures. In their monograph \emph{Distance-Regular Graphs}, Brouwer, Cohen, and Neumaier conjectured that every amply regular graph with $μ>1$, except the icosahedron, satisfies ${\rm{diam}}(G)\le2k/(λ+2)$. We confirm this bound when $μ>λ+1$ and give counterexamples to the conjecture with $μ=λ$. For amply regular graphs with $μ\geλ$ and $μ>1$, we obtain ${\rm{diam}}(G)\le 2k/μ+1$. This proves the Qiao--Park--Koolen conjecture. In 1983, Terwilliger conjectured that every $(s,c,a,k)$-graph with $c>1$ is finite. We prove this conjecture when $s>2$, $c>2$, and $(s,c)\ne(4,3)$. Moreover, we prove Weetman's finiteness conjecture for locally strongly regular graphs when the local parameter $μ>1$, and disprove his stronger conjecture that every strongly regular graph is an $\mathscr{S}$-graph. We also prove that every graph whose local graphs all have rank 3 is finite, which in particular proves a conjecture of Soicher in 1992.

entry.title: On an exponent-preserving duality for Coxeter multiarrangements of type $B_2$
entry.summary: In the theory of hyperplane arrangements, the study of logarithmic derivation modules is one of the most important subjects. If the module is free over a graded ring, the multiset of degrees of its homogeneous basis is called exponents. We utilize some basic theory of linear algebra to study the exponents of multiarrangements. As an application, we show a new exponent-preserving duality for the Coxeter multiarrangements of type $B_2$, which was conjectured by Torsten Hoge.

entry.title: Log-concavity of longest increasing subsequence
entry.summary: We prove a conjecture proposed by Chen that, for every fixed $n$, the sequence $(a_{n,k})_{k=1}^n$ is log-concave, where $a_{n,k}$ counts permutations of $[n]$ whose longest increasing subsequence has length $k$.

entry.title: Fuglede's conjecture holds in eight dimensions over the field with two elements
entry.summary: Fuglede's conjecture in a finite abelian group says that a nonempty subset tiles by translation if and only if it is spectral, meaning that the space of complex-valued functions on the subset has an orthogonal basis consisting of restrictions of group characters. We prove the conjecture in the eight-dimensional vector space over the field with two elements. In fact, every spectral set and every tile in this space has a tiling complement which is a linear subspace. We first prove that the Fourier support of a nonempty proper subset of density different from one half contains a two-dimensional subspace. Consequently, every spectral set of density one quarter has a subspace tiling complement. This gives a simpler proof of Kadowaki's dimension-seven result, replacing his use of the classification of Hadamard matrices of order 32 by the classical five classes of order 16. Our dimension-eight proof uses exact finite verifications involving Hadamard matrices of order 32 and perfect codes of length 15. We include the proofs of the reductions used from Kadowaki's preprint, so that neither positive result depends on his dimension-seven theorem. Finally, we give an elementary spectral example of density one eighth in dimension nine whose Fourier support contains no three-dimensional subspace. Thus, the Fourier-support argument at quarter density does not extend in this form to eighth density. Dimension nine is the only case still unresolved over the field with two elements, and this obstruction shows why the present Fourier-support method cannot resolve it as it stands.
entry.arxiv:comment: 22 pages. Programs, data, certificates, and verification logs are included as ancillary files. Standalone treatment of selected results from the preliminary preprint arXiv:2610.30712, with a new, simpler dimension-seven proof

entry.title: Realizing graph automorphisms as geometric symmetries of straight line drawings
entry.summary: Given a finite graph $G$, we characterize the automorphisms and automorphism groups of $G$ that can be realized as geometric symmetries and symmetry groups of straight line drawings of $G$ in the plane. In doing so, we correct a previous version of this characterization from the literature. As an application, we show that the graphs recently constructed by the first two authors to disprove the Polycirculant Conjecture, which have orders $16{,}464^k$ for each positive integer $k$, are the first known vertex-transitive graphs with no non-trivial realizable geometric symmetries. We also construct infinite families of graphs that exhibit all possible kinds of geometric symmetry.

entry.title: Cops and Robbers on Graphs without Long or Short Holes
entry.summary: In 2019, Sivaraman conjectured that every $P_k$-free graph has cop number at most $k-3$ for $k\geq 5$. Chudnovsky, Norin, Seymour, and Turcotte proved $P_5$-free graphs have cop number at most $2$. For $k\geq 6$ Sivaraman's conjecture remains widely open. There is little evidence to believe Sivaraman's conjecture is optimal, making the discovery of substantially better bounds interesting, even for subclasses of $P_k$-free graphs. We consider this problem for graphs with no long holes, which generalizes $P_k$-free graphs, that also have some forbidden shorter holes. Specifically, we show that for $t\geq 13$, $(C_4,\dots, C_{t}, C_k,C_{k+1},\dots)$-free graphs have cop number at most $\lceil \frac{k-2}{\lfloor \frac{t}{4}\rfloor }\rceil+1$. Taking $C_{k-1}$, which has cop number $2$ whenever $k\geq 5$, demonstrates that this bound is tight up to a small constant factor for infinity many pairs $k$ and $t$. The proof relies on showing that in graphs without short holes, the closed neighbourhood of a short induced path can be guarded by $1$ cop, even when these paths are not geodesics. Additionally, for $t\geq 2$ we show that $(C_{t+2},C_{t+3},C_k, C_{k+1},\dots, )$-free graphs have cop number at most $(t-1)\lceil \frac{(k-2)}{t}\rceil$. This show that $(C_4,C_5,C_k,C_{k+1},\dots)$-free graphs have cop number at most $\lceil \frac{k-2}{2}\rceil$, extending work by Clow and Meger on $(P_k,\text{claw}, \text{butterfly}, C_4,C_5)$-free graphs to a substantially more general class.

entry.title: Characterizing $3$-graphs with Degenerate Codegree Turán Density
entry.summary: Determining the Turán densities $π(F)$, uniform Turán densities $π_{\therefore}(F)$, and codegree Turán densities $γ(F)$ of $3$-graphs $F$ is a notoriously difficult problem in combinatorics. A landmark result by Erdős characterized the $3$-graphs whose Turán density is zero. Half a century later, Reiher, Rödl, and Schacht characterized the $3$-graphs whose uniform Turán density is zero. Recently, Ding, Lamaison, Liu, Wang, and Yang suggested a possible characterization of $3$-graphs whose codegree Turán density is zero, proved one direction of it, and conjectured the other. In this work we confirm this conjecture, completing the characterization of $3$-graphs with codegree Turán density zero. A particular difficulty of this result is that it is known that there are $3$-graphs with arbitrarily small codegree Turán density, contrasting the behavior of the normal and the uniform Turán density. Similar results were independently announced by Chen, Fang, and Yang.
